name: Omics capture: quench in place, metabolite flow-through per lane, capsules on to module 4 - module6_v1
source: Chip geometry, flows and volumes are ours. Depth-weir retention after Harrison/Oleschuk weir bead traps (US 7,312,611), as cited in contracts/blocks.json.
description: Runs on chip/module6_v1.json, one lane at a time (neurons, glia, astrocytes), each through its own inlet, chamber and outlet so the populations never mix. Per lane: hold the capsules behind the depth weir, flush with cold acidic organic solvent in place, collect that flow-through to the lane's own outlet for metabolomics, flush with a neutralising wash, then backflush the capsules on to module 4. The capsule shell is a nucleic-acid filter, not a protein sieve: the flow-through is a metabolite fraction, not a proteome. Mild lysis and cold-solvent quench are mutually exclusive, so only metabolome plus transcriptome are taken from the same capsules. Every volume is a multiple of the chamber's volume_ul (12.6 uL) or of the wetted lane volume (14.029 uL: chamber plus lines); every flow is the largest that keeps tau = 6 mu Q / (w h^2) at or below 0.01 dyn/cm2 with 15% headroom (mu = 0.8e-3 Pa s, w = 14 mm, h = 0.3 mm, giving 13.3 uL/min at 0.0084 dyn/cm2). The quench is in place but not fast: the front needs about 20 s to sweep the bed at that flow, against a pool turnover of about 1 s, so treat the metabolite data as unvalidated. Each lane holds about 44,901 capsules, about 3,456 cells, roughly 9x below the metabolomics floor. The solvent temperature and the flush multiples are placeholders to be fitted. The run file lays the lanes out in sequence; with three pump channels they could run in parallel because they share nothing wetted.

steps.note: Neurons: the lane's own selector valve is at its capsule feed and the capsules settle against the depth weir in cap_n, where they are held. A slurry concentrated off chip to near the packing limit fills the chamber in one chamber volume; a dilute slurry needs proportionally more. The other two lanes are capped and stay untouched.

Neurons: quench in place. The selector valve switches to the cold acidic solvent, which arrives by flow right where the capsules sit. The flow is the highest the shear ceiling allows, and the front still needs about 20 s to sweep the bed, so this is slower than the roughly 1 s pool turnover. The flow-through leaves by out_n to its own collection vial.

Neurons: close the collection vial. It holds the metabolite flow-through of this lane only, ready for metabolomics. It is NOT a proteome, because proteins mostly pass the capsule shell and nothing here is lysed mildly. The RNA stays in the capsules.

Neurons: the outlet valve now sends the flow to waste. A flush of the neutralising wash removes the acidic solvent from the capsules before the transcriptome workflow, and flushes the valve bore and lines to bound carry-over to the next step.

Neurons: hand-off. out_n is pressurised and in_n drains, so the flow runs backwards through the weir and lifts the capsules out through the lane's own line to module 4. The selector valve is at the module 4 position.
